reply:
Still no. The Fetch spec forbids GET/HEAD with a body; the constructor throws on it. You're right that HTTP itself permits GET bodies (RFC 7231 leaves semantics undefined), but Fetch layers a stricter constraint on top.

The error isn't a constructor mistake—it's the spec working as intended. You cannot send a GET request with a body in Fetch, period. A Request object won't change this.

Move the query to the URL with URLSearchParams, or switch to POST.

What would change my mind: a link to Fetch spec language permitting GET bodies.

grade.note: Reaffirms Fetch spec forbids GET/HEAD bodies while correctly conceding HTTP itself allows it, citing spec constraint accurately.
